patients.summary: High school history teacher with long-standing hypertension and type 2 diabetes who joined in 2019 and was steady on lisinopril and metformin for years, with untreated mixed hyperlipidemia. In late 2025 he developed acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, then thiazide-induced hypokalemia in February 2026; both settled, and amlodipine was added.

conditions.label: Essential hypertension
conditions.note: Diagnosed at prior practice; on lisinopril.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications
conditions.note: Diagnosed at prior practice; on metformin.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
50 y/o man transferring care; his last practice is closing its panel and he wanted a doctor he can text. Teaches history at the high school, starts back next week.

HTN for roughly six years, always on lisinopril, currently 20 mg once a day. Type 2 DM picked up about three and a half years ago on routine labs, metformin 1000 mg twice daily since, no lows, no GI trouble now. Has never been on insulin. No home glucose checks lately. Prior records requested.

No surgeries. NKDA.
Family: father with type 2 diabetes from age 58. Mother has high blood pressure and high cholesterol. Maternal grandfather had an MI at 65.
Social: has never used tobacco. A beer or two on weekends. Walks most evenings.

ROS negative, including vision, chest symptoms, urinary symptoms, foot numbness.

Exam: well, pleasant. BP and HR per vitals. BMI 30. Fundi not dilated. Thyroid normal size. Heart with regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs without crackles or wheeze. Abdomen soft. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt at all sites, dorsalis pedis palpable both sides. Legs without swelling.

A/P
1. Hypertension: at goal on lisinopril 20. Continue. BMP today.
2. Type 2 diabetes: A1c, fasting glucose, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Eye exam yearly, he will book with his optometrist.
3. Lipids drawn today as part of the baseline.
4. Prevention: Tdap given. Hep C and HIV screening today, he agreed. Due for colonoscopy at 50, referral placed to GI. PHQ-2 negative.

Return in about 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Derek, your baseline labs are back. Kidney function, blood counts and the urine protein test are all normal. A1c is in a good range for someone on metformin. Hep C and HIV screens are negative. Talk soon.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came by after school for his flu shot. No egg or vaccine reactions in the past, feels well today. Quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM given L deltoid. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, left in good spirits.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report (outside GI)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group. Procedure date 11/19/2019.
Indication: first screening colonoscopy, age 50, no family history of colon cancer.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril. Allergies: NKDA.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Prep: good, Boston-type score not recorded; adequate for polyps over 5 mm.
Findings: scope advanced to the cecum, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. Mucosa normal throughout. No polyps, masses or diverticula seen. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
Impression: normal screening exam.
Recommendation: next colonoscopy in 10 years.
Copy to referring primary care physician.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes / HTN Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Feels fine. Taking both meds every day, uses a weekly pill box. School is talking about closing because of the virus, he is a little stressed about remote teaching.
O: vitals reviewed, BP fine. Wt stable. Heart and lung exam normal. Feet look good.
A/P: T2DM on metformin and HTN on lisinopril, both doing well. A1c and BMP today. Refills sent for 90 days with 3 refills. Next visit in roughly 3 months, may do it by video if the office goes to remote visits.

documents.title: March labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, yesterday's A1c and kidney panel are back and line up with September. No changes. Stay well with everything going on.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Office limiting in-person visits this week. Called Mr. Conti, appointment cancelled, he will do a video visit in June instead. He has refills through summer.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is at his kitchen table, verbal consent for telehealth.
Spring was rough with remote teaching but he kept walking. Meds unchanged, no side effects, no low sugars. Home BP cuff readings mostly in the low 130s over low 80s, he read me a week of them.
March A1c and kidney panel reviewed with him, stable.
Plan: continue metformin 1000 twice a day and lisinopril 20. Eye exam this summer. In-person visit with labs in December.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Exam Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Community optometry practice. Exam date 08/11/2020.
Reason: annual dilated exam, type 2 diabetes.
VA corrected 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. IOP 15 / 16.
Dilated fundus exam: discs sharp and pink, vessels normal caliber, maculae flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization either eye.
Assessment: no diabetic retinopathy. Mild presbyopia, readers updated.
Return in 12 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Masked, screening questions negative at the door. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. No issues. Reminded him his diabetes visit is in December.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - DM/HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person for the first time since March. Teaching hybrid now. No complaints. Taking metformin and lisinopril as prescribed. Optometry letter from August reviewed: no retinopathy.

Exam: BP and pulse in range today. Weight unchanged. Cardiac and pulmonary exam normal. Feet: protective sensation present bilaterally, good pulses, nails trimmed, no calluses.

Plan: fasting labs drawn this morning (CMP, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin). Shingrix dose 1 today, he knows to expect a sore arm and maybe a tired day; second dose in 2 to 6 months. Same meds. Physical next year.

documents.title: Re: December labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, December labs are back. A1c is steady, kidney and liver tests normal, no protein in the urine. Keep doing what you're doing. The front desk will reach out about the second shingles shot.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix. After dose 1 he had an achy arm and felt run down for about a day, nothing more. Dose 2 given 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Series complete.

documents.title: COVID vaccine dates
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, teachers got moved up so I got both Moderna shots at the regional clinic, March 3 and March 31. Card photo attached. Second one knocked me out for a day but I'm fine. -Derek

documents.title: Re: COVID vaccine dates
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Derek, both doses added to your record from the card.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Last week of school. Says the year wore him down but health-wise nothing new. No hypoglycemia, no polyuria. Lisinopril and metformin every day.
Exam: BP ok on recheck. Lungs clear, heart regular rhythm. Feet unremarkable.
A1c and BMP drawn. Continue current regimen. Book eye exam for August. Physical around the holidays.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send new 90-day scripts for metformin and lisinopril? Pharmacy says no refills left. Also my eye appointment got pushed to the fall, they were backed up.

documents.title: Re: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Both renewed for a year and sent to your usual pharmacy. Thanks for the heads up on the eye visit.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Flu
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Asked about a COVID booster, eligible as of next month per current guidance; scheduled.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - COVID Booster
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Moderna booster (half dose, 0.25 mL) IM R deltoid. Watched 15 minutes, fine. Physical is scheduled for Dec 30.

documents.title: Annual Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, on school vacation. Mostly here to keep the diabetes on track. No complaints at all, sleeping fine, energy fine.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily. NKDA.
FH: father developed type 2 diabetes at 58.
SH: nonsmoker. Social drinker, weekends only.

Vitals: BP 132/85, HR 78. BMI 30.
General: comfortable, no distress.
HEENT, neck: normal; no thyroid enlargement or nodes.
CV: S1 S2 normal, no murmur.
Resp: clear throughout.
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Ext: no swelling. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses strong, skin healthy.
Neuro, skin: normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Fasting labs drawn before the visit: glucose 126, A1c 6.5%. Lipids TC 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 150.

A/P
- T2DM, controlled on metformin. Continue 1000 BID. Urine microalbumin pending.
- HTN on lisinopril 20, fine. Continue.
- Prevention: colonoscopy 2019 normal, Tdap 2019, Shingrix done, flu and COVID booster this fall. Eye exam got pushed; he will reschedule.
Follow up in about 6 months.
